How to read a gold buy signal

Gold just closed lower for the third day running. Is that a buying opportunity or a warning sign? Neither, really — it's just a pattern. Here's what GoldAlert's signal actually means, and just as important, what it doesn't.

Start with the rule, not the feeling

Three consecutive lower closes flips an asset to WATCH. Five flips it to STRONG. That's the whole mechanism — no hidden formula, no black box. We built it this way on purpose: a rule you can check by hand beats a "smart" model you have to trust blindly. Pull up any asset's price history and count the red days yourself. You'll land on the same answer the site does.

Why "consecutive," not "big drop"

A single ugly 4% day can look scarier than five quiet 1% declines in a row, but the streak rule cares about persistence, not size. There's a reason for that: a sustained pullback tends to reflect sentiment shifting over several sessions, while a one-day drop is often just noise — an earnings miss, a stray headline, a thin-volume afternoon. Neither is inherently more "buyable." They're different animals, and the streak rule only tracks one of them.

The optional minimum-drop filter

Some pullbacks are technically three red days but add up to almost nothing — a few cents here, a few cents there. If that kind of noise bothers you, set a minimum total decline and the tool ignores streaks that don't clear it. Leave it at zero and every qualifying streak counts, however small.

What the tier badge is not telling you

WATCH and STRONG label a pattern. They are not a prediction. The badge doesn't know whether this particular pullback is about to reverse or keep sliding — no rule does. Treat it the way you'd treat a smoke detector: worth a closer look, not an instruction.

Before you act on one

Pull up the asset's chart and actually look at it. Check the news. Glance at the backtest table for that specific asset — how has this exact rule performed on it historically, and how many times has it even fired? A signal built on three past occurrences tells you a lot less than one built on thirty. None of that turns a signal into advice, but it does turn a blinking badge into an informed decision.

This article explains how the tool works and is not financial advice.
